theme: General Knowledge Vol 2: Discoveries, Milestones & Global Wonder
title: General Knowledge Vol 2: Discoveries, Milestones & Global Wonder
description: Comprehensive 60-question grand master assessment exploring medicine, empires, earth landmarks, masterworks, physics, deep sea, mythology, aviation, megastructures, and philosophy.

questions.question: Which English physician published the first accurate description of the systemic circulation of blood pumped by the heart in 1628?
questions.explanation: William Harvey published De Motu Cordis in 1628, demonstrating that blood circulates continuously in a closed system.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body by both surface area and weight?
questions.explanation: The skin, or integumentary system, accounts for approximately 15 percent of total body weight and covers roughly two square meters.

questions.question: Which British biophysicist captured Photo 51, providing critical X-ray diffraction data for discovering the DNA double helix?
questions.explanation: Rosalind Franklin obtained Photo 51 at Kings College London in 1952, which clearly revealed the helical nature of DNA.

questions.question: Which human blood type is considered the universal red blood cell donor for emergency transfusions?
questions.explanation: Type O-negative red blood cells lack A, B, and Rh antigens, minimizing the risk of adverse immune reactions in recipients.

questions.question: What is the longest, heaviest, and strongest single bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur or thighbone extends from the hip to the knee joint and can support up to thirty times an adult body weight.

questions.question: What is the average resting heart rate in beats per minute for a healthy adult at rest?
questions.explanation: A normal resting heart rate for healthy adults typically ranges between 60 and 100 beats per minute, averaging roughly 72 bpm.

questions.question: Which decisive battle fought in October 1066 led to the Norman conquest of Anglo-Saxon England?
questions.explanation: Duke William of Normandy defeated King Harold Godwinson at Hastings, beginning centuries of Norman rule in Britain.

questions.question: Which Macedonian king defeated Persian Emperor Darius III at the Battle of Gaugamela in 331 BCE?
questions.explanation: Alexander the Great employed brilliant tactical maneuvering at Gaugamela to overthrow the Achaemenid Persian Empire.

questions.question: In what year did Ottoman forces led by Sultan Mehmed II breach the defensive walls of Constantinople?
questions.explanation: The siege and fall of Constantinople on 29 May 1453 marked the end of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire.

questions.question: Which landmark constitutional charter was signed by King John of England at Runnymede in 1215?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta established the principle that everyone, including the sovereign king, is subject to the rule of law.

questions.question: Which historic battle in 490 BCE saw Athenian hoplites defeat a Persian invasion force, inspiring the modern marathon run?
questions.explanation: Athenian forces crushed the Persian expedition at the plain of Marathon, after which a runner famously carried word of victory to Athens.

questions.question: In what year CE was the monumental Hagia Sophia completed and consecrated in Constantinople under Emperor Justinian I?
questions.explanation: Justinian I inaugurated the grand domed basilica of Hagia Sophia on 27 December 537 CE.

questions.question: What South American waterfall in Venezuela is the highest uninterrupted waterfall on Earth?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls plunges 979 meters from the Auyan-tepui mountain, with an uninterrupted single drop of 807 meters.

questions.question: What is the world largest salt flat, spanning over 10,000 square kilometers high in southwest Bolivia?
questions.explanation: Salar de Uyuni was formed by prehistoric lake transformations, creating an extraordinary natural mirror when covered in water.

questions.question: Which African lake is the deepest lake in Africa and the second deepest freshwater lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika reaches a maximum depth of approximately 1,470 meters and contains 16 percent of global surface fresh water.

questions.question: What island nation in the North Atlantic Ocean is famous for geysers, active volcanoes, and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift?
questions.explanation: Iceland sits directly atop the divergent tectonic boundary between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.

questions.question: Which mountain pass at the border of Pakistan and Afghanistan served as a historic military and trade corridor for millennia?
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass traverses the Spin Ghar mountains and was a strategic chokepoint on the northern Silk Road.

questions.question: What is the official elevation in meters of Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain summit in Africa?
questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is a dormant stratovolcano rising to an elevation of 5,895 meters above sea level.

questions.question: Which Renaissance master spent four years painting the monumental Genesis frescoes on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512 under the commission of Pope Julius II.

questions.question: Which German Baroque master composed the celebrated six Brandenburg Concertos in 1721?
questions.explanation: Johann Sebastian Bach presented the six instrumental concertos to the Margrave of Brandenburg-Schwedt in 1721.

questions.question: Which French sculptor created the famous bronze masterpiece The Thinker in 1904?
questions.explanation: Auguste Rodin conceived The Thinker as part of his monumental commission The Gates of Hell depicting Dante Alighieri.

questions.question: What classical Greek temple dedicated to the goddess Athena crowns the Acropolis of Athens?
questions.explanation: Built under the statesman Pericles in the 5th century BCE, the Parthenon represents the pinnacle of classical Doric architecture.

questions.question: Which Russian Romantic composer wrote the ballet masterpieces Swan Lake, The Nutcracker, and The Sleeping Beauty?
questions.explanation: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky composed beloved orchestral scores that defined the golden age of classical Russian ballet.

questions.question: In what year was the Eiffel Tower officially inaugurated in Paris as the entrance arch for the 1889 World Fair?
questions.explanation: Gustave Eiffel opened the 330-meter wrought-iron lattice tower on 31 March 1889 for the Exposition Universelle.

questions.question: Which theoretical physicist formulated the General Theory of Relativity published in 1915?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein revolutionized modern physics by describing gravitation not as a force, but as curvature of spacetime caused by mass.

questions.question: Which Russian chemist published the first recognized Periodic Table of Elements arranged by atomic mass in 1869?
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev organized known elements and successfully predicted the physical properties of yet-undiscovered elements.

questions.question: What is the theoretical temperature at which all fundamental thermal motion of particles ceases, defined as zero Kelvin?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero corresponds to zero on the Kelvin thermodynamic scale, equivalent to minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What fundamental law of physics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another?
questions.explanation: The First Law of Thermodynamics, or the law of conservation of energy, is a fundamental invariant of physical systems.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of sound in dry air at 20 degrees Celsius at sea level?
questions.explanation: Acoustic sound waves travel through dry air at 20 degrees Celsius at approximately 343 meters per second (1,235 km/h).

questions.question: What is the boiling temperature of pure water in degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: Under standard 1-atmosphere sea-level pressure, pure liquid water boils and transitions to steam at 100 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: Which marine mammal holds the record as the largest known animal ever to have existed on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Blue Whale (Balaenoptera musculus) can reach masses exceeding 190 metric tons, far surpassing any known dinosaur.

questions.question: Which Australian coastal marvel is the largest living coral reef ecosystem on Earth, visible from space?
questions.explanation: Stretching over 2,300 kilometers off Queensland, the Great Barrier Reef comprises over 2,900 individual coral reefs.

questions.question: Which cephalopod boasts the largest eyes of any living creature, measuring up to 27 centimeters in diameter?
questions.explanation: The Colossal Squid possesses massive bioluminescent-detecting eyes designed to spot predatory sperm whales in the deep sea.

questions.question: What deep-sea hydrothermal structures vent mineral-rich sulfide waters exceeding 350 degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: Black smokers form along volcanic spreading centers, supporting chemosynthetic ecosystems independent of solar sunlight.

questions.question: What is the main structural component that forms the hardened exoskeletons of crustaceans and insects?
questions.explanation: Chitin is a tough nitrogen-containing polysaccharide polymer that provides structural rigidity to arthropod shells.

questions.question: What is the maximum recorded body length in meters of a mature Blue Whale?
questions.explanation: The largest recorded blue whales measured up to 30 meters (roughly 98 to 100 feet) from rostrum to fluke.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, what immense sacred ash tree connects and supports the nine cosmos realms?
questions.explanation: Yggdrasil is the central world tree in Norse cosmology, with roots extending to the well of Urd, Niflheim, and Jotunheim.

questions.question: Which ancient Mesopotamian narrative inscribed on clay tablets is widely recognized as the world earliest surviving epic poem?
questions.explanation: The Epic of Gilgamesh recounts the legendary King of Uruk quest for immortality, dating back to the Third Dynasty of Ur.

questions.question: Which jackal-headed deity was worshipped in ancient Egypt as the god of mummification and the afterlife?
questions.explanation: Anubis presided over the embalming rituals and guided souls to the Hall of Maat for the Weighing of the Heart.

questions.question: According to classical Greek mythology, which peak was revered as the home of the Twelve Olympian gods?
questions.explanation: Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in Greece, was believed in ancient times to be the divine court of Zeus and the gods.

questions.question: Which Roman sea god corresponds directly to the Greek Olympian god Poseidon?
questions.explanation: Neptune was the Roman deity of freshwater and the sea, traditionally depicted wielding a three-pronged trident.

questions.question: How many famous heroic labors was the Greek demigod Heracles tasked with performing for King Eurystheus?
questions.explanation: Mythological tradition establishes the Twelve Labors of Heracles, including slaying the Nemean Lion and the Lernaean Hydra.

questions.question: Who made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight from New York to Paris aboard the Spirit of St. Louis in 1927?
questions.explanation: Charles Lindbergh completed the 33.5-hour solo flight across the Atlantic Ocean on 20–21 May 1927, winning the Orteig Prize.

questions.question: Which Norwegian explorer led the first expedition to reach the geographic South Pole in December 1911?
questions.explanation: Roald Amundsen and four team members reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911, five weeks ahead of Scotts party.

questions.question: Which ocean liner struck an iceberg on its maiden voyage and sank in the North Atlantic in April 1912?
questions.explanation: The White Star Line ship RMS Titanic collided with an iceberg and sank on the night of 14–15 April 1912 with heavy loss of life.

questions.question: Which supersonic passenger jet airliner operated commercial transatlantic flights at over Mach 2 from 1976 to 2003?
questions.explanation: Jointly developed by Britain and France, Concorde carried passengers from London and Paris to New York in under 3.5 hours.

questions.question: Who led the 16th-century Spanish expedition that achieved the first recorded maritime circumnavigation of the globe?
questions.explanation: Ferdinand Magellan initiated the voyage in 1519, and Juan Sebastian Elcano completed the historic global voyage aboard the Victoria in 1522.

questions.question: What was the cruising top speed in kilometers per hour of the supersonic Concorde airliner?
questions.explanation: Concorde cruised at Mach 2.04, equivalent to approximately 2,179 km/h (1,354 mph), at an altitude of 60,000 feet.

questions.question: What 50-kilometer railway tunnel beneath the Strait of Dover connects Folkestone, England with Coquelles, France?
questions.explanation: Opened in 1994, the Channel Tunnel possesses the longest undersea portion of any tunnel in the world at 37.9 kilometers.

questions.question: Which iconic orange suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate strait in California opened to traffic in 1937?
questions.explanation: Designed by Joseph Strauss, the Golden Gate Bridge spans 2.7 kilometers and is internationally recognized by its International Orange hue.

questions.question: Which massive particle physics laboratory in Geneva, Switzerland operates the Large Hadron Collider?
questions.explanation: The European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) operates the LHC to explore fundamental subatomic particles like the Higgs boson.

questions.question: What massive hydroelectric gravity dam spanning the Yangtze River in Hubei, China is the world largest power station by installed capacity?
questions.explanation: The Three Gorges Dam has an installed capacity of 22,500 megawatts and generates over 100 terawatt-hours of electricity annually.

questions.question: Which 82-kilometer artificial waterway across Central America connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, opening in 1914?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal utilizes a stepped system of lock chambers that lift ships 26 meters up to Gatun Lake and down to sea level.

questions.question: What is the total circumference in kilometers of the Large Hadron Collider circular underground tunnel ring at CERN?
questions.explanation: The LHC occupies a circular tunnel 26.7 kilometers (commonly cited as 27 km) in circumference buried up to 175 meters beneath the Franco-Swiss border.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization of southern Mesopotamia developed the cuneiform script, one of the earliest writing systems?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians developed cuneiform wedge-shaped marks pressed into soft clay tablets around 3400 BCE.

questions.question: Which classical Athenian philosopher was sentenced to death in 399 BCE by drinking poisonous hemlock for corrupting the youth?
questions.explanation: Socrates accepted the Athenian court verdict in 399 BCE, choosing philosophical integrity over flight from the city.

questions.question: What planned international auxiliary language was created in 1887 by ophthalmologist L. L. Zamenhof?
questions.explanation: Zamenhof published Unua Libro under the pseudonym Doktoro Esperanto, aiming to create an easy-to-learn universal second language.

questions.question: Which Swedish industrialist and inventor of dynamite endowed the prestigious international Nobel Prizes in his 1895 will?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel bequeathed his fortune to establish annual awards in Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, and Peace.

questions.question: What ancient library in Ptolemaic Egypt was one of the largest and most significant scholarly archives of the ancient world?
questions.explanation: The Great Library of Alexandria was founded in the 3rd century BCE under the patronage of the Ptolemaic dynasty.

questions.question: How many total Nobel Prize categories are officially awarded annually according to the Nobel Foundation?
questions.explanation: Six Nobel awards are conferred: the original five established by Nobel (Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace) plus Economic Sciences added in 1968.
